builder: OCD's source import (live-private importer and sanitizer), from the value's source families

findings.basis: Three groups. (1) US carriers, Telekom DE and O2 DE come from OEM device trees: Qualcomm's CAF carrier template (Linux Foundation copyright, 2016) in many trees, plus OnePlus or Nothing additions for 262-01 and 262-03. The Sony Open Devices entries are the same template (entry date 2020-07-02). These files go with Qualcomm's own IMS stack, not with the AOSP ImsStack. (2) Several profiles are no real operator: 310-00, 310-01, 310-02, 310-88, 311-00, 310-80 and 310-90 are template entries with two-digit MNCs, and 'Carrier 31001/31002/31088/31100' list no family. (3) KT, SK Telecom and LG U+ (open.450006) come from AOSP's carrier files (carrier IDs 1890 to 1892). These are real carrier settings, and Korean operators are known to support video emergency reports. Google's CarrierSettings sets this key for no carrier in the kodiak set, so the Google lane serves the default false for all 41 profiles.
findings.effect: With true, TelecomAccountRegistry adds CAPABILITY_EMERGENCY_VIDEO_CALLING whenever the SIM has video calling (TelecomAccountRegistry.java:479-481). Telecom then keeps a video emergency request as video (CallsManager.java:2257-2264), and ImsPhoneCallTracker no longer downgrades it (ImsPhoneCallTracker.java:1781-1786). The emergency call reaches the AOSP ImsStack as a video call. ImsCallApp builds an emergency profile with video for SERVICE_TYPE_EMERGENCY (ImsCallApp.java:368-390), and getCallTypeByImsState keeps CALL_TYPE_VT for emergency (ImsCallApp.java:428-441). The INVITE to the emergency service then offers video. ImsStack adds the video feature tag to the emergency registration only when its own imsemergency.support_video_for_ereg_bool is set (CarrierConfig.h:1806-1812, AosNConfiguration.cpp:1777-1778). No OCD source sets that key. The stock Dialer hides the video button for emergency numbers in the call log (CallLogListItemViewHolder.java:480-498), so the path opens mainly through other apps' video intents. On failure, the emergency redial on another domain is forced to audio (TelephonyConnectionService.java:3431). On this S20, video calling is live: build 9 set config_device_vt_available=true, and IMS registers mmtel video with o2 (STATUS.md:139-153). For O2 DE, OCD also sets carrier_vt_available_bool true. So the owner's own SIM would take this path.
findings.risk: Against the otherwise served false, true can only add risk. A video emergency request becomes a video INVITE from the AOSP ImsStack, on the emergency PDN, without a video tag in the emergency registration. That path was never tested on this stack. The S20's video media is proven only in loopback, not against a real far end (STATUS.md:153,176), and the radio reports no QoS bearers, so no video bearer can be confirmed. No German or US emergency service is known to take video. An E-CSCF or PSAP gateway that rejects the offer, instead of answering with video port 0, makes the first attempt fail: the 112 call is delayed or lost until the audio redial. With false, the same request is placed as a plain audio emergency call. That outcome is the only one the project can rely on, because no emergency call can be tested.

notes: Hold for all 41 profiles. The value changes how an emergency call is placed: as video instead of audio. On LineageOS with the AOSP ImsStack it would send video emergency INVITEs over a path nobody has tested, on a phone where video is now enabled for the owner's own o2 SIM. For most profiles the basis is a Qualcomm or OEM template meant for another IMS stack, and some profiles are no real network. The Korean values from AOSP are real carrier settings, but the stack risk is the same, so they are held too. CarrierSettings should keep serving the default false (emergency calls downgraded to audio). Read in the 23.2 tree; the phone runs 24.0, not re-checked.
